Proposition
[Compactness of closed subgroups] 1. 9.1.6\group thurston.ch09.convergenceSource: thurston:page-0244 For every Lie group $G$, its space of closed subgroups is compact in the geometric topology.
Proof

\sketch If small nonidentity elements have a uniform lower bound, diagonal compactness of the bounded finite sets gives a discrete limit. Otherwise select the maximal limiting subspace of infinitesimal directions; it is closed under Lie brackets, and the same diagonal argument gives a closed subgroup with that tangent space.

□
